pull_request.title: feat: implement excessive_vec_capacity lint
pull_request.body:
Closes #46

## Summary

Adds a lint that flags `Vec::with_capacity(N)`, `.reserve(N)`, and `.reserve_exact(N)` calls where `N` is a hard-coded integer literal above `1024`.

The Soroban SDK's own `Map`/`Vec`/`Bytes` don't expose a capacity-reservation API, so this targets plain Rust `Vec` (`std`/`alloc`) used for local scratch computation inside a contract. Unlike a long-running server process, a Soroban guest Wasm instance runs against a small, hard-capped linear memory budget (see [Cost Rationale — Memory](docs/cost_rationale.md#2-memory-ram)): the allocation is charged the moment it's made, regardless of whether the capacity is ever filled. A large, hard-coded literal that isn't tied to a known input bound is a structural sign of over-allocation.

Non-literal arguments (e.g. `Vec::with_capacity(input.len())`) are intentionally **not** flagged — they're already tied to a runtime-computed bound, which is exactly the fix this lint suggests.

## Implementation details

- `ExcessiveVecCapacity` is a `check_expr` pass matching two call shapes:
  - `Vec::with_capacity(N)` — an `ExprKind::Call` whose callee resolves (via `cx.qpath_res(...).opt_def_id()`) to a function ending in `vec::Vec::with_capacity`.
  - `v.reserve(N)` / `v.reserve_exact(N)` — an `ExprKind::MethodCall` whose receiver type (via `cx.typeck_results()`) is an ADT ending in `vec::Vec`.
- The literal argument is extracted via `LitKind::Int(value, _) => value.get()` (same pattern `clippy_utils::consts` uses), so `1024`, `1024usize`, and `1_024` all resolve to the same numeric value regardless of suffix/underscores.
- **Non-obvious bug I hit and fixed along the way:** `rustc_middle::ty::TyCtxt::def_path_str` embeds the enclosing impl block's generic parameter list for associated functions on generic types — `Vec::with_capacity` prints as `alloc::vec::Vec::<T>::with_capacity`, not `alloc::vec::Vec::with_capacity`. The existing `match_soroban_def_path` helper's plain suffix match can't see through that (it's only ever been used against ADT type paths and non-generic-impl functions before now, so this never came up). Rather than change that shared, already-relied-upon helper, I added `strip_generic_segments` (removes bracketed `<...>` segments and collapses the resulting empty path segment) plus a `match_generic_fn_path` wrapper, used only by this new lint's `Call` arm.
- `EXCESSIVE_VEC_CAPACITY_THRESHOLD` is a `u128` constant (`1024`) so it composes with `LitKind::Int`'s `u128` value type without truncation concerns.

## Files

**New:**
- `docs/lints/excessive_vec_capacity.md` — lint reference page.

**Modified:**
- `soroban_cost_lints/src/lib.rs` — `ExcessiveVecCapacity` late lint pass, `strip_generic_segments`/`match_generic_fn_path` helpers, `LINT_METADATA`/`register_lints` wiring (category: `Memory`).
- `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` / `ui/main.stderr` — new UI fixtures (see Tests below).
- `README.md`, `docs/lints/README.md`, `docs/cost_rationale.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` — lint listed under Memory with rationale and target-resource summary.

**Test files:** all under `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.rs` (fixtures) / `soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr` (expected diagnostics), following this repo's existing UI-test convention.

## Tests added

All in the new `excessive_vec_capacity — Fixtures` section of `ui/main.rs`:

- `bad_vec_with_capacity_literal` — `Vec::with_capacity(10_000)` → **warns**.
- `bad_vec_reserve_literal` — `.reserve(5000)` → **warns**.
- `bad_vec_reserve_exact_literal` — `.reserve_exact(2048)` → **warns**.
- `good_vec_with_capacity_small_literal` — `Vec::with_capacity(16)` (below threshold) → no warning.
- `good_vec_with_capacity_from_input_len` — `Vec::with_capacity(input.len())` (non-literal) → no warning.
- `good_vec_new_grows_incrementally` — `Vec::new()` + `.push()` in a loop (no reservation at all) → no warning.
- `allowed_vec_with_capacity_literal` — same over-capacity case suppressed via `#[allow(excessive_vec_capacity)]` → no warning.

## How to test

```bash
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace
```

All three pass locally. The UI test (`cargo test -p soroban_cost_lints`) exercises the new fixtures against the bundled `ui/main.stderr` expectations.

commits.message:
feat: implement excessive_vec_capacity lint

Flag Vec::with_capacity(N), .reserve(N), and .reserve_exact(N) calls
where N is a hard-coded integer literal above 1024. Soroban's guest Wasm
instance runs against a small, hard-capped linear memory budget, so a
large capacity reservation is charged the moment it's made regardless of
whether it's ever filled — unlike a long-running server process where
over-reserving is cheap. Non-literal arguments (e.g. input.len()) are
left alone since they're already tied to a runtime-computed bound.

- Add ExcessiveVecCapacity late lint pass matching both the free-function
  call form (Vec::with_capacity) and the method-call form (.reserve/
  .reserve_exact), using typeck results to confirm the receiver/return
  type is std/alloc's Vec.
- Add strip_generic_segments/match_generic_fn_path helpers: rustc's
  def_path_str embeds the enclosing impl's generic parameter list for
  associated functions on generic types (e.g. `Vec::<T>::with_capacity`),
  which a plain suffix match against the existing match_soroban_def_path
  helper can't see through.
- Add UI fixtures covering all three flagged call forms, a small literal,
  a non-literal (input-derived) capacity, incremental growth via
  Vec::new(), and an #[allow] suppression case.
- Document the lint in docs/lints/excessive_vec_capacity.md, the README
  feature list, docs/lints/README.md, docs/cost_rationale.md, and
  CHANGELOG.md.

Closes #46

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' into feat/excessive-vec-capacity

# Conflicts:
#	soroban_cost_lints/ui/main.stderr

fix: resolve CI build failures in SARIF output and fixture workspace

- SarifRun.results was typed Vec<SarifResult> while the SARIF result
  builder constructed plain serde_json::Value objects via json!(),
  a leftover mismatch from a prior merge that broke compilation.
  Retype results as Vec<serde_json::Value>, drop the now-dead typed
  Sarif* structs, and wire the already-collected rule descriptors
  into tool.driver.rules.
- integration.rs used HashSet<String> but inserted &str literals;
  fix the declared type.
- alpha/beta fixture crates each declared their own [workspace]
  while also being listed as members of the parent workspace,
  causing cargo metadata to fail with "multiple workspace roots
  found". Drop the redundant per-crate [workspace] tables.

These were the actual cause of the "SARIF result missing level"
CI failures reported on PRs #232, #267, #269, #270 (all inherited
the same broken merge state) — the binary failed to compile, it
was not a runtime field-mapping bug.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
